newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds were lower at the close of trade, as Confederate bond futures dipped on profit-taking following recent gains.

The declines were tied partly to a drop in German Bunds following comments by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing, who said in a television interview that there was no need to further lower key German interest rates.

One Swiss trader said volume was greater in the futures than in the underlying cash. Selling took December Conf futures back towards support at 114.80. If that level holds, the contract may target 115.20 again, the trader said.
Retail customers were seen largely absent from the market.
Late in the day prices of shorter maturities also came under moderate pressure, traders said.
The Swiss National Bank releases the advance version of its monthly report on Thursday. The report includes data on Swiss money supply growth.

Short-term rates had declined on Tuesday when SNB vice president Jean-Pierre Roth said monetary policy should be used to offset any Swiss franc appreciation resulting from EMU. Analysts saw his comments as an indication that SNB policy is likely to remain expansive.
Dec Conf futures CONFZ6 down 47 at 114.82.
Dec Comi medium-term bond COMIZ6 down 24 at 110.21.
Dec Euro Swiss francs FESZ6 down two at 98.26.
